AR = correlation past errors
MA = correlation past shocks/noise (moving average)
ARMA(p,q)
p = number of AR (AutoRegressive) terms 
q = number of MA (Moving Average) terms
Different ARMA structures decide how many past timepoints and how many past shocks matter.


*Huitema* 
A flexible approach involves specifying a *four-parameter regression model* that provides 
> estimates of level change and slope change from the first phase to the second.
> estimation usually can be carried out using either conventional ordinary least squares (OLS) or, if autocorrelated errors are present and 
large samples are available, generalized least squares (GLS). 

*parameters*
- phase 1 intercept
- phase 1 slope
- level change (immediate effect after intervention)
- slope change (change in slope after intervention)
*slope-change var*
this var will be 0 in baseline phase, because *df$D  (D = 0 in baseline)
first point of intervention  = 0 as well, because n1 = number of obs in baseline
it counts the difference in time since the start of intervention

### full 4 parameter model
model_full <- lm(Y ~ T + D + slope_change_var, data = df)
summary(model_full)

### output
Y=β0+β1T+β2D+β3[(T−(n1+1))D]
β₀ = Phase‑1 intercept
β₁ = Phase‑1 slope
β₂ = level change
β₃ = slope change.
> Phase‑2 slope = β₁ + β₃  
coef(model_full)["T"] + coef(model_full)["slope_change_var"]

It is assumed that the errors of the model possess the following properties:
1. Independence. The value of each error is statistically independent of all other
errors. In the case of a time-series design, it is assumed that errors before and
after the error at time t contain no information (beyond that provided by the
mean of the errors) that is useful in predicting the error at time t. --> *checks for AR!!*
2. Constant variance. Regardless of the level of the X variable(s) included in the
model, the associated process errors have a common variance. --> *homosced* 
3. Identical distributions. The process errors associated with each level of the X
variable(s) are identically distributed.

# prepare data for analysis (tb)
not done: removal of dates after
Dummy needed for later calculation (time since intervention)
needed to make a numerical (nrow) time indication for later calculation for slope-change var
```{r}
# remove B17 (excluded from study)
tb<-tb[tb$Completed==1,]
#tb<-tb[!tb$Studienummer %in% c("B21", "B23_original")]
table(tb$Studienummer)
table(tb$sent_date > tb$T3_Evaluatiegesprek_date) # not removed single case analysis

### phase indicator 
# create dummy for intervention phase 
tb$intervention_fse <-if_else(tb$phase_FSE=="A", 0, 1)
tb$intervention_satisf_health<-if_else(tb$phase_satisf_health=="A", 0, 1)

# time indication (nrow in time)
#class(tb$sent)
  tb <- tb %>%
  group_by(Studienummer) %>%
  mutate(
    nA_SF = sum(intervention_satisf_health == 0),
    slope_change_satis_health = (time - (nA_SF + 1)) * intervention_satisf_health,
    nA_FSE = sum(intervention_fse == 0),
    slope_change_fse = (time - (nA_FSE + 1))* intervention_fse
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
  
```

## AR 1 FSE -------------------------------------------
B14_fse_imp_full_ar1 <- gls(fse_imp ~ time + intervention_fse + slope_change_fse,
                 correlation = corARMA(p=1, q=0, form = ~ time),

# normalized residuals
resid <- residuals(B14_fse_imp_full_ar1, type = "normalized")

# assumption checks

acf(B14_fse_imp_full_ar1) 
pacf(B14_fse_imp_full_ar1)

qqnorm(resid[B14$intervention_fse == 1])

# FSE (imp and orig)
```{r}
# ── Settings ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
studienummers <- unique(tb$Studienummer)   # all unique IDs
#dep_var       <- "fse_imp"                 # dependent variable label for table
dep_var       <- "fse"                 # dependent variable label for table

# ── Output containers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
results_list <- list()

# ── Loop ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
for (id in studienummers) {

  cat("Processing:", id, "\n")

  # 1. Subset data
  dat <- tb[tb$Studienummer == id, ]

  # 2. Fit ARMA(1,1) model
  model <- tryCatch(
    gls(as.formula(paste(dep_var, "~ time + intervention_fse + slope_change_fse")),
        correlation = corARMA(p = 1, q = 1, form = ~ time),
        data = dat,
        na.action = na.omit),
    error = function(e) {
      message("  Model failed for ", id, ": ", e$message)
      return(NULL)
    }
  )
  
  if (is.null(model)) next

  # 3. Normalized residuals
used <- as.integer(rownames(model$data))  # rows kept after na.omit
res  <- residuals(model, type = "normalized")
fit  <- fitted(model)
 pre  <- dat$intervention_fse == 0
  post <- dat$intervention_fse == 1
  
  # 4. Save assumption plots to PDF ──────────────────────────────────────────
  pdf_path <- file.path(OutDir, paste0(id, "_ITSA_assumptions_", dep_var, ".pdf"))
  pdf(pdf_path, width = 8, height = 6)

  # ACF / PACF
  acf(res,  main = paste(id, "– ACF normalized residuals"))
  pacf(res, main = paste(id, "– PACF normalized residuals"))

  # Homoscedasticity
  plot(res ~ fit,
       xlab = "Fitted values", ylab = "Normalized residuals",
       main = paste(id, "– Residuals vs Fitted"))
  abline(h = 0, lty = 2, col = "grey50")

  # QQ plots
  qqnorm(res,       main = paste(id, "– QQ: all"))
  qqline(res)
  qqnorm(res[pre],  main = paste(id, "– QQ: pre-intervention"))
  qqline(res[pre])
  qqnorm(res[post], main = paste(id, "– QQ: post-intervention"))
  qqline(res[post])

  # Histograms
  hist(res,       main = paste(id, "– Hist: all"),       xlab = "Normalized residuals")
  hist(res[pre],  main = paste(id, "– Hist: pre"),        xlab = "Normalized residuals")
  hist(res[post], main = paste(id, "– Hist: post"),       xlab = "Normalized residuals")

  dev.off()
  cat("  Plots saved to:", pdf_path, "\n")

  # 5. Extract model summary table ───────────────────────────────────────────
  s      <- summary(model)
  coef_m <- s$tTable   # columns: Value, Std.Error, t-value, p-value

  coef_df <- data.frame(
    Studienummer  = id,
    dep_var       = dep_var,
    term          = rownames(coef_m),
    estimate      = round(coef_m[, "Value"],     2),
    std_error     = round(coef_m[, "Std.Error"],  2),
    t_value       = round(coef_m[, "t-value"],    2),
    p_value       = signif(coef_m[, "p-value"],   2),
    # ── extra useful info ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
    n_obs         = s$dims$N,
   # logLik        = round(as.numeric(logLik(model)), 2),
   #AIC           = round(AIC(model), 2),
   # BIC           = round(BIC(model), 2),
    row.names     = NULL
  )

  results_list[[id]] <- coef_df
}

# 6. Combine into one table ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
results_table <- do.call(rbind, results_list)
rownames(results_table) <- NULL

# 7. Inspect / save ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
print(results_table)

fse_orig<-results_table
#fse_imp<-results_table
#fse_imp<-bind_rows(fse_imp, fse_B14)

```

# health and satisfaction
```{r}
# ── Settings ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#studienummers <- unique(tb$Studienummer)   # all unique IDs
dep_var       <- "health"
#dep_var       <- "health_imp"
#dep_var       <- "satisfaction"
#dep_var       <- "satisfaction_imp"



# ── Output containers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
results_list <- list()

# ── Loop ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
for (id in studienummers) {

  cat("Processing:", id, "\n")

  # 1. Subset data
  dat <- tb[tb$Studienummer == id, ]

  # 2. Fit ARMA(1,1) model
  model <- tryCatch(
    gls(as.formula(paste(dep_var, "~ time + intervention_satisf_health + slope_change_satis_health")),
        correlation = corARMA(p = 1, q = 1, form = ~ time),
        data = dat,
        na.action = na.omit),
    error = function(e) {
      message("  Model failed for ", id, ": ", e$message)
      return(NULL)
    }
  )
  
  if (is.null(model)) next

  # 3. Normalized residuals
used <- as.integer(rownames(model$data))  # rows kept after na.omit
res  <- residuals(model, type = "normalized")
fit  <- fitted(model)
pre  <- dat$intervention_satisf_health == 0
post <- dat$intervention_satisf_health == 1

  # 4. Save assumption plots to PDF ──────────────────────────────────────────
  pdf_path <- file.path(OutDir, paste0(id, "_ITSA_assumptions_", dep_var, ".pdf"))
  pdf(pdf_path, width = 8, height = 6)

  # ACF / PACF
  acf(res,  main = paste(id, "– ACF normalized residuals"))
  pacf(res, main = paste(id, "– PACF normalized residuals"))

  # Homoscedasticity
  plot(res ~ fit,
       xlab = "Fitted values", ylab = "Normalized residuals",
       main = paste(id, "– Residuals vs Fitted"))
  abline(h = 0, lty = 2, col = "grey50")

  
  # QQ plots
qqnorm(res, main = paste(id, "– QQ: all"))
qqline(res)
if (sum(!is.na(res[pre])) > 1) {
  qqnorm(res[pre], main = paste(id, "– QQ: pre-intervention"))
  qqline(res[pre])
} else {
  plot.new(); title(paste(id, "– QQ: pre — insufficient data"))
}
if (sum(!is.na(res[post])) > 1) {
  qqnorm(res[post], main = paste(id, "– QQ: post-intervention"))
  qqline(res[post])
} else {
  plot.new(); title(paste(id, "– QQ: post — insufficient data"))
}

# Histograms
hist(res, main = paste(id, "– Hist: all"), xlab = "Normalized residuals")
if (sum(!is.na(res[pre])) > 1) {
  hist(res[pre], main = paste(id, "– Hist: pre"), xlab = "Normalized residuals")
} else {
  plot.new(); title(paste(id, "– Hist: pre — insufficient data"))
}
if (sum(!is.na(res[post])) > 1) {
  hist(res[post], main = paste(id, "– Hist: post"), xlab = "Normalized residuals")
} else {
  plot.new(); title(paste(id, "– Hist: post — insufficient data"))
}

  dev.off()
  cat("  Plots saved to:", pdf_path, "\n")

  # 5. Extract model summary table ───────────────────────────────────────────
  s      <- summary(model)
  coef_m <- s$tTable   # columns: Value, Std.Error, t-value, p-value

  coef_df <- data.frame(
    Studienummer  = id,
    dep_var       = dep_var,
    term          = rownames(coef_m),
    estimate      = round(coef_m[, "Value"],     2),
    std_error     = round(coef_m[, "Std.Error"],  2),
    t_value       = round(coef_m[, "t-value"],    2),
    p_value       = signif(coef_m[, "p-value"],   2),
    # ── extra useful info ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
    n_obs         = s$dims$N,
 #   logLik        = round(as.numeric(logLik(model)), 2),
#    AIC           = round(AIC(model), 2),
#    BIC           = round(BIC(model), 2),
    row.names     = NULL
  )

  results_list[[id]] <- coef_df
}

# 6. Combine into one table ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
results_table <- do.call(rbind, results_list)
rownames(results_table) <- NULL

# 7. Inspect / save ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
print(results_table)


health_orig<-results_table
#health_imp<-results_table
#satisfaction_orig<-results_table
#satisfaction_imp<-results_table


```



# save the output 
```{r}
# Create a new workbook
wb <- createWorkbook()

# List of dataframes
dfs <- list(
  fse_imp = fse_imp,
  health_imp = health_imp,
  satisfaction_imp = satisfaction_imp,
  fse_orig = fse_orig,
  health_orig = health_orig,
  satisfaction_orig = satisfaction_orig
)

# Loop over list and add each to its own sheet
for (name in names(dfs)) {
  addWorksheet(wb, name)
  writeData(wb, sheet = name, dfs[[name]])
}

# Save the workbook
saveWorkbook(wb, file = paste0(OutDir, "2026-04-01_ITSA-output.xlsx"), overwrite = TRUE)

```
